text:
Alex: Hey Jordan, you got a minute? I'm trying to figure out whether to refinance my loans.
Jordan: Sure. What do you have?
Alex: A car loan, twelve thousand left at nine percent, and student loans, twenty-eight thousand at, I think, six and a half. And I've got a decent credit score now, seven-ten or so.
Jordan: With seven-ten you can probably get the car loan down to six or seven. Have you checked with a credit union?
Alex: Not yet. I looked at one online lender, they quoted seven point two. But there's an origination fee, um, one percent.
Jordan: A one percent fee on twelve thousand is a hundred twenty bucks. If you save two points over three years, that's, what, about three hundred forty a year, so it's worth it.
Alex: Right. The student loan, though, is federal, and I heard if you refinance it privately you lose the protections.
Jordan: Yeah, you lose income-driven repayment and forbearance options. At six and a half it's not terrible. I'd leave it unless you can get like four.
Alex: Okay. That makes sense. So just the car loan.
Jordan: And check for a prepayment penalty on the current one before you switch.
Alex: Good point. I'll call them tomorrow. Thanks, man.
Jordan: Anytime.

metadata.note: friend call: considering refinancing a student loan and a car loan
